subject: Midnight validator failure during control-plane upgrade — bridge summary
messages:
From: Tom Berger <tom.berger@healthwise.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: Sana Ahmed <sana@healthwise.com>
Date: Sun, 7 Mar 2027 02:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nightly upgrade impact — control-plane validator failed (HealthWise)

Irene / Laura,

We saw an availability blip in our private VPC deployment during the 00:30 UTC maintenance window. Our telemetry shows a series of failed healthchecks against the control-plane validator and a subsequent spike in customer 502s for ~18 minutes. We opened the incident on our side and escalated to our ops team.

High level:
- Start: 00:33 UTC, first 502s observed
- Peak failure window: 00:33–00:51 UTC
- Impact: user requests queued, some API calls retried and timed out

We suspect the recent control-plane upgrade you ran yesterday rolled a validator pod that failed liveness checks and then blocked the management-plane reconciliation for a rolling window. Can you confirm if you rolled the 1.6.3->1.7.0 validator image in our cluster?

We need:
1) Short summary of what happened and immediate mitigations you took.
2) Logs for the validator pod(s) around 00:20–01:10 UTC (compressed).
3) A proposed rollback/fix plan and ETA.

Sana will be on point for HealthWise. This is causing a handful of customer incidents and we need a bridge asap.

Thanks,
Tom Berger
Director, Platform Engineering
HealthWise

[Attachment: screenshots_control_00-51.png (image/png) referenced]

---
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Tom Berger <tom.berger@healthwise.com>, Sana Ahmed <sana@healthwise.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 7 Mar 2027 02:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nightly upgrade impact — control-plane validator failed (HealthWise)

Tom / Sana,

Thanks for the quick heads up and the screenshot. We saw the same error surface in our upgrade telemetry and confirmed a failed validator rollout in your Private control plane during the 00:30 UTC window. Immediate actions taken:
- Halted the automated rolling update at 00:38 UTC and pinned the validator image to the previous stable revision (1.6.3).
- Performed a controlled restart of the leader validator at 00:42 UTC which restored reconciliation services at 00:51 UTC.
- Re-enabled normal traffic routing at 00:55 UTC.

We are packaging logs and a short timeline now. Can we do a 30-minute bridge to walk through the logs and agree on a remediation and postmortem? Proposed bridge: today 09:00 UTC (11:00 local for you). I will include our upgrade engineering and SREs.

Preliminary root hypothesis: an intermittent liveness probe regression in the 1.7.0 validator image combined with tighter readiness gating in your private cluster. We are pulling full pod logs, kube-apiserver events, and systemd journals and will upload them to the shared Drive.

Attachments I will include for the bridge: logs_0307.tar.gz (validator logs + kube events), timeline_0307.csv (service-level timeline), and the debug screenshot you sent.

Irene Choi
Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

---
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Tom Berger <tom.berger@healthwise.com>, Sana Ahmed <sana@healthwise.com>
Date: Sun, 7 Mar 2027 03:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nightly upgrade impact — control-plane validator failed (HealthWise)

Joining notes from the on-call SRE side: we saw the validator container crash-loop during image init (OOM-ish stack in the runtime). We collected:
- /var/log/containers/validator-*.log (included in logs_0307.tar.gz)
- kubelet and kube-apiserver events (included)
- metrics: small spike in CPU throttling for the validator sidecar (logs indicate GC pauses)

Mitigation summary:
- Rollback to 1.6.3 completed at 00:43 UTC.
- Temporary increase of readiness probe timeout to avoid aggressive restarts while we triage.

We'll discuss a longer-term mitigation on the bridge (possible new liveness probe config, resource limits tuning, and a gating test in the canary pipeline).

Laura Bennett
Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: logs_0307.tar.gz (application/gzip) attached]

---
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Tom Berger <tom.berger@healthwise.com>, Sana Ahmed <sana@healthwise.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident summary and next steps — validator rollout regression (HealthWise)

Tom / Sana / HealthWise team,

Thank you for your patience while we completed our internal investigation and cross-checked with the upgrade pipeline. This message is the post-incident summary and the action items we committed to during the bridge on 2027-03-07.

What happened (concise):
- During the scheduled upgrade window at 00:30 UTC on 2027-03-07 we rolled the control-plane validator from image 1.6.3 -> 1.7.0.
- The 1.7.0 image contains a change to the runtime lifecycle that reduced the default readiness probe timeout; under the cluster's current pod-resource limits the validator process sometimes took longer to initialize and failed the liveness probe.
- The failed validator led to a short interruption of control-plane reconciliation which caused client requests to receive 502s while the management-plane recovered. Total customer-facing impact: ~18 minutes between 00:33–00:51 UTC.

Root causes:
1) Image regression: 1.7.0 default readiness/liveness defaults are too aggressive for some resource-constrained environments.
2) Canary gap: our canary pipeline did not exercise pods with the same resource constraint profile as your private cluster.
3) Probing config: the upgrade gated on container readiness but did not include a ramped timeout for first-start.

Immediate fixes we implemented (already in place):
- Reverted your control-plane validators to 1.6.3 during the incident; rollback verified at 00:43 UTC.
- Updated our upgrade runbook to increase initial readiness timeout for validator pods by default during first-start on private deployments.
- Added a pre-upgrade check that validates the canary against a sampling of customer resource profiles.

Planned follow-ups (with owner and ETA):
- Engineering: ship a 1.7.1 validator image with corrected probe defaults and reduced memory footprint. Owner: Marcus Lin. ETA: 2027-03-29.
- QA: extend canary matrix to include low-memory and low-CPU pod profiles. Owner: Laura Bennett. ETA: 2027-03-24.
- Product/Operations: add an opt-in staged rollout with a 1-hour warm window for Private customers. Owner: Ben Carter. ETA: 2027-04-05.

Artifacts attached to this thread:
- logs_0307.tar.gz: validator logs, kube events, and node journals (sha256: abc123def...).
- timeline_0307.csv: minute-level timeline of events and recovery actions.
- controlplane_screenshot.png: customer-provided 502 screenshot.

Relevant tickets and references:
- Internal: INF-4872 (upgrade validator default probe regression)
- Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_example_drive_link (logs and raw captures)

Compensation / credits: As discussed on the bridge, we will issue a goodwill credit for the impacted API calls and an exemption on the monthly SLA measurement for March. Your Growth lead will follow up with the formal credit memo under deal HW-7892.

If you want a formal PDF postmortem for your audit records, we can produce one and include the signed timeline and log bundle. Please let me know.

Again, apologies for the disruption and thank you for the quick coordination. We will text/emailed Marcus and Laura if we detect any related anomalies during the upcoming staged rollout.

Best,
Irene Choi
Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
irene@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198
